target_customer: Finance teams at companies that make high volume vendor, contractor and marketplace payouts
problem: Businesses pay vendors and contractors with checks, spreadsheets and ad hoc tools. Routable automated payables and mass payouts from invoice receipt to settlement.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payment volume fees
product_category: B2B payments and accounts payable automation

founders.name: Omri Mor
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no education or employers.

founders.name: Tom Harel
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background. The company's Series A post says the founders previously built custom B2B payout systems for clients and interviewed over 150 CFOs and finance leaders.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments orchestration across partner banks, compliance, tax forms and accounting integrations is standard fintech engineering with regulatory and bank partner hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: Deep accounting integrations, onboarding and compliance workflows and bank partnerships raised switching costs, though many competitors offered similar payables features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not absorb the wedge per sources; Anchorage Digital, a crypto bank, acquired Routable in October 2026 to add fiat and stablecoin payout rails.

market_need_then: The founders interviewed over 150 CFOs and finance leaders before building; payables remained manual for many finance teams.

rebrands.why: Not stated by sources; trademark for Routable was filed October 2018 by Warren Payments, Inc.
Company blog says it launched a completely new look and feel to capture attention and foster trust.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear descriptive coinage and a 2024 visual refresh, but no sources show mascot, community or brand press; a different startup named Routable AI exists and can be confused with it.

outcome_analysis: Routable came out of stealth in August 2020 with a $12M Series A and raised a $30M Series B led by Sam and Jack Altman in April 2021, reaching about 160 staff. It was acquired by Anchorage Digital in October 2026 at an undisclosed price, which fits a strategic payments buy rather than an IPO track outcome. Whether investors profited is not public.
notes: Finextra says $16M raised at the August 2020 launch, of which $12M was the Series A; the other roughly $4M is unaccounted for, so coverage is partial. Totals vary by aggregator (ZoomInfo $42M, CB Insights $48M, press $46M after Series B). A $0.49M Series B extension in 2022 is from one tracker and not recorded. Search sources say the company began as Warren in Seattle; the rename date is not sourced beyond the October 2018 trademark filing. Competitor search returned only current vendor comparison pages, so the list is empty. Anchorage announcement date of October 6 comes from one secondary report.
